kitDescription: Naga is an Electric shotgun Supporter (Burst II) whose job is to make the team's core hits hurt more. While she fires, every few shots she hands the two highest-ATK allies a +40.07% core-damage buff for 5 seconds and heals the two lowest-HP allies for 9.58% of her own max HP, and every 12 shots she repairs the whole team's cover. If an ally puts a shield on her, she upgrades that support massively: all allies get +85.17% core damage for 10 seconds each time a shield lands on her. Her burst gives herself Pierce for 10 seconds and grants every ally a flat attack boost worth 16.18% of her own ATK for 10 seconds — plus a second boost worth another 31.02% of her ATK if a shield is on her at the moment she bursts. With no shielder in the squad, the two biggest lines of her kit (the +85.17% core damage and the +31.02% ATK) simply never turn on, and she is left as a modest core-damage and ATK support.

redAssertions: s2a 'the trigger counts ROUNDS, not SG pellets' (procs = coreBuffs(40.07)/2 must be <= 120): REAL divergence. The driver's override is kit-literal (hitCount count:5), but the engine increments hitCount by hitsPerShot (SG = 10 landed pellets/shot, sim.ts:2905), so the block fires ~1.5x per SHOT (~300+ procs/180 s) instead of once per 5 shots (~45). Blind S5 and blind S6 and the S2b fable spec ALL independently read the prose as rounds; the driver kept the engine's SG convention and documented it. This is the only RED that maps to a real prose-vs-behavior gap.

s1b 'exists and is GATED, not absent' (delete requiresShielded -> 85.17 fires): fails because the driver keys s1b to the {kind:'shielded'} APPLICATION trigger, not a requiresShielded state gate. Not a driver defect — the blind S6 author flagged this exact alternative themselves ('if the engine has a shield-application trigger ... re-key skill1[0]'), and the cross-family S2b review independently ruled 'Activates WHEN a Shield is set' = application-triggered. RECON_ERROR against the driver.

'naga casts her own burst' (non-vacuity, >=4 casterAtkPct applies): fails on the PRISTINE fixture only — controlComp('naga') seats crown (cd 20, leftmost B2) ahead of naga, so naga takes 0 Burst-II casts and every burst assertion in the blind file is vacuous. Blind fixture defect; the driver's re-seating is the correct repair.

s1b 'is INERT with no shield source in the comp': fails on the PRISTINE fixture only — crown's burst emits a shield, contradicting the blind author's own stated premise that liter/crown/naga/helm contains no shielder. Blind fixture defect, self-contradictory as written.

gotchas.summary: The engine's hitCount counts LANDED PELLETS for a shotgun (increments by hitsPerShot), so naga's two 'after 5 normal attack(s)' blocks fire ~1.5x per SHOT instead of once per 5 shots — roughly 10x the prose cadence.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Activates after 5 normal attack(s).' Engine: hitCount += hitsPerShot per shot (sim.ts:2905); naga hitsPerShot 10, rate_of_fire 90 (40 f/shot), ammo 9, reloadFrames 111. Driver: kept count:5 and documented 'hitCount counts hits; kept parser-faithful' (override note) + A4 in the adapted test header. Blind S6: authored count:5 as ROUNDS and ⚑-flagged the alternative ('if the engine counts SG pellet HITS instead, the 5-hit S2 fires ~10x more often'). S2b fable: named pellet-counting THE nearest-wrong misread and demanded a cadence pin against shot events — which is precisely the S5 assertion the driver had to remove (A4). Both cross-family derivations read the prose as ROUNDS.
gotchas.suggestedFix: No per-unit patch — do NOT compensate by changing count:5, which is kit-literal. This is a repo-wide `hitCount` semantics question for multi-pellet weapons and needs an owner ruling: does 'after N normal attack(s)' mean N trigger pulls (rounds) or N landed hits? Naga's own damage exposure is ~nil (worst rounds-based inter-proc gap = 4x40+111 = 271 f = 4.5 s, inside the 5 s buff window; only the first proc shifts, ~3.3 s -> ~0.4 s), but the ruling is load-bearing for every SG/MG hitCount carrier and for the heal's recovery-feed rate. Recipe if measurement is wanted: focus-video naga, count buff-icon appearances of the 40.07% core buff against her ammo counter over one magazine — 1 appearance per ~5 rounds confirms ROUNDS, ~1-2 per round confirms HITS.

gotchas.summary: The 9.58% heal is modeled as an amountless recovery EVENT, and 'the 2 allies with the lowest HP percentage' resolves to the leftmost 2 slots — so which teammates receive the recovery feed is a slot artifact, not a kit-driven choice.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Affects 2 ally unit(s) with the lowest HP percentage. Recovers 9.58% of the skill user's final Max HP as HP.' Engine: the `heal` effect carries no HP amount (prika precedent) and v1 has no HP pool, so 'lowest HP%' is indeterminate. Driver caveat records both. S2b independently warned: 'the stand-in choice must be shown damage-inert UNLESS an on-recovery consumer sits in a specific slot — then which 2 units receive the heal IS load-bearing.'
gotchas.suggestedFix: Leave as-is for naga (byte-identical in the graded comp, and the driver's crown probe puts the consumer inside the leftmost 2 by construction). Needs measurement/primitive work, not a number: (a) an HP-pool primitive before 'lowest HP%' can resolve honestly; (b) if any future comp seats an on-recovery consumer outside slots 0-1, re-verify the feed reaches it rather than assuming. Never pick recipients to move a total.

verdictRationale: All seven kit lines are either FAITHFUL (4) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (3) — there is no SILENT_DROP, no ENCODING error, and no undocumented divergence anywhere in this override. Ranked findings: (1) the SG hitCount rounds-vs-pellets semantics, which is a real prose-vs-engine gap, is documented by the driver, is engine-wide rather than naga-specific, and is nearly damage-inert here because the rounds-based 4.5 s worst-case proc gap already sits inside the 5 s buff window; (2) the amountless heal + leftmost-2 stand-in for 'lowest HP%', documented and blocked on an HP-pool primitive. Convergence is mechanically RED, but it decomposes cleanly and none of it counts against the driver: two red assertions are defects in the blind author's own fixture (crown monopolises the Burst-II slot so naga never casts, and crown emits a shield that contradicts the blind's own 'no shield source' premise), one is the s1b trigger disagreement where the blind author FLAGGED their own choice as provisional and the cross-family S2b fable review independently ruled for the driver's shielded-application trigger, and only the cadence bound is a genuine finding — the one the driver had to relax (A4) and recorded for this packet rather than hiding. The driver is in fact the only one of the three derivations that applies both shield primitives distinctly ('when' -> shielded event trigger, 'if' -> requiresShielded state gate), which is exactly what the mechanics SSOT §9 specifies. Discrimination is sound: every load-bearing line carries a counterfactual that moves the board (gate delete leaks the 31.02 line; alliesTopAtk -> allies reaches 4 targets; casterAtkPct -> atkPct moves the carry; count 5 -> 200 drops the total; heal removal collapses crown's recovery buff ~70x), and the two skipped assertions are honest v1 GAPs (cover-HP pool, pierceDamagePct inert) that the blind author skipped for the same reasons. Nothing must change for GO. Same-model residual the owner should spot-check: both opus blinds AND the fable review read 'after 5 normal attack(s)' as trigger pulls while the shipped engine counts landed pellets — three derivations agreeing on the prose reading and the engine doing something else is the one place where agreement is not evidence, so the hitCount-for-multi-pellet-weapons convention deserves an explicit owner ruling (buff-icon-vs-ammo-counter read on a naga focus video is the cheap instrument); secondarily, the s1 85.17% uptime remains a ⚑ inherited from the modeled shielder cadence and is unmeasured against real in-game shield uptime.
